feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader with clear public-sector specialization and solid evidence of scope, progression, and technical breadth. It reads professionally and is mostly polished, but it is somewhat dense, slightly repetitive across skills sections, and could sharpen outcomes to increase impact.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong career progression at NACo, culminating in director-level ownership of web, analytics, governance, and multimedia.  
- Good credibility signals: concrete scale metrics (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers) and relevant tools/platforms strengthen trust.  
- Strong positioning: headline, summary, and project examples consistently support a niche in enterprise digital modernization for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to save space and improve scannability.  
- Add more outcome-focused results: several bullets describe responsibilities well, but more quantified business/user impact would strengthen impact (e.g., engagement gains, efficiency improvements, adoption, cost/time savings).  
- Tighten writing consistency: use parallel bullet structure and consistent punctuation around lists. Minor style issues include “social, and multimedia” (remove comma), “Ranked among the top public universities…” (unnecessary filler), and mixed styling such as “A2/Learning,” “AI-enabled,” and title case choices like “Coleman DAVIS.” No major misspellings or grammar errors found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible positioning with clear seniority and sector focus, but it overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. It would be stronger with one sharper value proposition and fewer broad capability lists.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten to one concise branding statement plus one impact-focused sentence; emphasize public-sector scale and modernization outcomes.
- Replace “Leads” with “Experienced leading” or make both sentences parallel in tense/style.
- Add one concrete scale cue from recent roles (for example, 10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers) to increase specificity.
- Possible rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing web platforms, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector organizations. Experienced leading enterprise website transformation, analytics and reporting infrastructure, editorial systems, and multimedia programs—including AI-enabled search and content experiences—for complex, mission-driven teams.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies and recent projects; consider narrowing this to “AI-enabled search and content experiences.”
- The long list of functions repeats skills already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes that align with the headline and recent roles, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with Topline Skills and the header. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize leadership-level capabilities rather than repeating detailed skill categories.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Reframe as higher-level, outcome-oriented competencies: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and content operations • Analytics, reporting and optimization • AI-enabled search and discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Replace “editorial systems” with “content operations” for clearer executive-level language.
- Change “Multi-channel communications operations” to “Multi-channel digital communications leadership” if you want stronger seniority signaling.
- Standardize phrasing style: use either all noun phrases or all “X and Y” constructions.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with Header and Topline Skills; consider reducing this section to 6–7 items.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” is repeated across Work Experience and Technical + IT.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads like an expanded repeat of the recent consulting/NACo experience. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it more distinctive and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Rename to “Selected Recent Projects” and keep each item to one sharp line with parallel structure.
- Add scope, audience, or outcome where possible (for example: legislative content discovery, campaign growth, conference engagement, recurring advocacy cadence).
- Tighten wording: “hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search, and bill-level AI chat” is strong; simplify longer phrases like “modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.”
- Standardize style and punctuation across entries; spell out “10-by-20-foot” for consistency.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search and the microsite closely repeat the current freelance role bullets; consider making the footer more portfolio-like by emphasizing project names, formats, or outcomes not stated above.
- Advocacy Video Series overlaps with multiple NACo roles; keep only if you can add a distinct result or scale.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader

Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a broad responsibility list rather than a high-impact recent engagement. Tighten it around 3–4 outcomes and avoid repeating NACo-era themes already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + client type + value: “Embedded full-time as strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements across web, campaigns, content operations, and analytics.”
- Replace generic verbs with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Built cross-functional workflows and reporting systems to improve coordination across organization-wide communications.”
- Combine Drupal/CMS bullets into one sharper line: “Designed and launched Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- Make the AI/search work the standout final bullet and add metrics if available: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and user-facing discovery features for complex policy/member content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, usability, and operational best practices” overlaps with the NACo Director role; keep only if you can show a distinct result.
- CMS/front-end troubleshooting is too tactical unless tied to scale, launch speed, or performance gains.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact role with solid scale metrics; it should read more like an executive achievement entry and less like a responsibility summary. Emphasize transformation, team leadership, and business outcomes while trimming channel-management detail already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opening sentence with an outcome-led summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget, leading platform modernization and organization-wide communications operations.”
- Tighten bullets to 4–5 achievement-focused points; e.g., “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible for email/social/video/analytics: growth %, production volume, reporting speed, engagement lift, cost savings, or reduced reliance on vendors.
- Use stronger verbs and parallel structure: led, built, expanded, standardized, established.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the prior NACo role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video studio/buildout may overlap with footer projects; mention the studio here, save recurring series details for projects or earlier roles.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong scope and clear progression, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like responsibilities than outcomes. Tighten it to emphasize what changed under your leadership at this level before the later director role.

Suggested edit:
- Open with impact + scope: “Led NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging for county officials nationwide.”
- Combine newsletter bullets and add outcome if available: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders, improving consistency, cadence and cross-team alignment.”
- Make the video bullet more active: “Launched and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a repeatable policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague workflow language with a concrete systems angle: “Built stronger editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing coordination and content consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital communications across web, email, social and video” is repeated in the Director role; keep this version focused on execution/scale, not team oversight.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the earlier NACo role; frame this entry as expansion/operationalization, not initial creation.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and work experience. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and distinct strengths rather than repeating broad communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less generic phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience strategy and content planning
- Consider swapping “messaging” for “communications” to sound more senior and operationally grounded.
- If space allows, make one line more outcome-oriented, e.g. “Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector platforms.”
- Keep terms aligned with recent roles: governance, operations, enterprise web, and cross-channel leadership are stronger than general content wording.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is somewhat covered by recent experience; avoid adding “storytelling” here since it appears elsewhere.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it’s too long and overlaps heavily with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. For a topline section, make it sharper, more current, and oriented to platforms plus execution strengths most supported by recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Drupal • CMS modernization & migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations • Workflow automation • AI-enabled search experiences
- Drop older/lower-signal items here: remove WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, Airtable systems, and jQuery unless they are central to target roles.
- Replace generic labels with stronger phrasing: “CMS modernization” → “Drupal platform modernization & migration”; “Workflow automation” → “Workflow automation & system integration.”
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work elsewhere, e.g., “10,000+ page Drupal migration” rather than listing more tools.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates Technical + IT almost line-for-line; keep Topline Skills broader and reserve tool inventory for Technical + IT.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating it in multiple headline sections unless it’s a target-role differentiator.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value capability themes over repeating platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics strategy & reporting” rather than just products.
- Tighten to 5–6 items and group tools: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio & Power BI” instead of listing each separately.
- Add outcome-oriented language where possible: “KPI framework design,” “executive dashboarding,” “performance and search insights.”
- Suggested rewrite: “- Analytics strategy & KPI framework design - Executive and leadership dashboarding - GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio & Power BI - User behavior analysis with Microsoft Clarity - SEO, content performance & optimization insights”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep Topline Skills strategic and leave the fuller tool inventory there.
- “Leadership reporting” overlaps with “analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies; use a sharper phrase like “executive dashboarding.”

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies plus several NACo bullets. Make it more specific to delivery scope and systems expertise rather than repeating broad video capability.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio Systems & Event Delivery**
- Tighten content to: **Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and webcast delivery • PTZ camera and studio system operation • Hybrid, virtual and in-person event production**
- If space allows, add one higher-value qualifier tied to recent work: **Built and operated in-house studio workflows for advocacy programming and live events**
- Keep terms outcome-/scope-oriented; “broadcast-quality” and “webcast delivery” signal level better than “editing” and “studio operations”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Video production and editing” is partly redundant with Technical + IT tools (Premiere Pro, Audition, podcast production).
- “Livestreaming” duplicates Core Competencies wording; use “livestream and webcast delivery” or “studio systems” to differentiate.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too generic and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either add proficiency/context or be trimmed to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to show depth and recency, e.g. “Drupal (enterprise/public-sector web modernization), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages.”
- Put the most relevant platform first and consider de-emphasizing older/lighter-use tools: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint | Working knowledge: Power Pages, GitHub Pages.”
- If accurate, add scale/context instead of just names: “Drupal (10,000+ page migration; microsites), WordPress, SharePoint.”
- Keep formatting consistent with other technical lists; avoid a standalone CMS list if the same tools already appear elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists Drupal, WordPress, and SharePoint.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel low-signal unless tied to a project or removed for space.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, analytics, automation, and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End & Technical Implementation
- Rewrite as: JavaScript, HTML5, CSS3, jQuery • API and tag implementation • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions / deployment automation
- Consider grouping by function rather than listing flat tools; this makes it feel more senior and execution-focused.
- If accurate, add one concrete qualifier in a nearby project/role bullet instead of here, e.g., “built custom front-end components,” “implemented tracking via GTM,” or “automated deployments with GitHub Actions.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” already appears under Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing in both places.
- “API integrations” and automation themes also overlap with Core Competencies and recent experience, so keep this item tool-specific rather than strategic.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow design capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize capability, e.g. “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools.”
- Group by function for faster scanning: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams.”
- Keep only tools that support your recent systems/governance work; consider dropping older or lower-signal items if space is tight.
- If format allows, add one short qualifier instead of a pure list, e.g. “Used to build editorial workflows, intake systems, approvals and cross-team coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing elsewhere.
- Slack/Teams are low-impact unless tied to operational systems; they may dilute stronger technical tools.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a bare vendor list and misses the operational/email leadership already shown in recent NACo roles. Make it clearer, tighter, and aligned to platform administration and campaign execution rather than generic “engagement.”

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Communications Platforms
- Rewrite as: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, strengthen with function-based phrasing: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (campaign automation) • Higher Logic (member email/community communications) • Mailchimp (newsletter deployment)
- If one platform was primary in recent roles, list that first to reflect recency and depth.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about leading email newsletters and digital channels; keep this section tool-focused only, not responsibility-focused.
- “Engagement” is vague and may duplicate broader “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is highly duplicative of “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” In the Technical + IT section, make it more tool-specific and tighter, leaving strategy terms to the topline section.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Google Search Console • A/B testing tools
- Replace broad nouns like “Dashboarding” with a platform or capability already evidenced elsewhere, e.g., “reporting dashboards” only if needed.
- Consider swapping “SEO” for “Google Search Console” or “technical SEO” to make the item more concrete and technical.
- Order by strongest/recently evidenced tools from the NACo role: GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, BigQuery.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps almost exactly with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; keep Topline strategic (KPI design, leadership reporting, performance analysis) and this section purely tool-based.
- “A/B testing” is not supported elsewhere in the CV; keep it only if you can cite a real example or outcome in recent experience.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize “firsts,” scope, and team-building contributions from this earlier stage.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to stress foundational impact: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital media function supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add clearer ownership and outputs: “Supported a major website refresh; produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates; improved day-to-day publishing and production workflows.”
- Tighten the management phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised daily work of a digital media associate.”
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email/social volume supported, or workflow/time savings.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; distinguish this as launching/producing the series rather than expanding it.
- Avoid repeating broad “strengthened workflows across web, email, social” language already used in later NACo entries.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and underplays the most distinctive achievement: launching NACo’s first podcast. Since later roles already cover broad digital/media leadership, this item should stay concise and emphasize foundational innovation and multimedia ownership.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county-focused programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the podcast the second sentence and tighten phrasing: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Replace “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” with something more active and specific, e.g. “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications and research dissemination.”
- If possible, add scope: number of episodes, audience, or cross-team partners.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad “digital content/multimedia” language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overstate leadership here in ways that overlap with the 2015–2024 digital management progression.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful supporting skills, but this item currently mixes software with capabilities and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tighten it into named tools plus one concise production qualifier.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Podcast recording/editing • Livestream studio production”
